extracted.intended_audience: policy analysts, IP statisticians, patent office officials, researchers and other stakeholders interested in patenting activity and indicators
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, indicators and explanatory notes used to measure and report global patenting activity (e.g., patent families origin/destination, resident vs non-resident filings/grants, patents in force, utility models, PCT activity, and related growth/share metrics). Useful for producing or interpreting patent statistics and comparisons across offices/countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of patent families by country of origin and destination office
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of patent families by countries of origin (owner of the invention) and destination office (five largest patent offices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides indication of ownership of the invention and the region where the owner wishes to protect the invention. Example observations: many families originating from Japan and the Republic of Korea contain USPTO filings and a significant proportion contain filings at China's SIPO; 59% of families originating from Canada contain USPTO filings (reflecting geographic proximity and market size); European-origin families tend to have a high share with EPO filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total patent grants (trends, 1985-2006)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time series of total patent grants worldwide and associated year-on-year growth rates for 1985–2006.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to track global grant volumes; interpretation should account for patent office capacity/resources (e.g., examiners, IT infrastructure) which influence grant numbers. Example note: 2006 saw ≈727,000 grants (18.2% increase), partly due to efforts to reduce backlog and increases in grants from China and the Republic of Korea. Grants trend is more volatile than filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of resident vs non-resident patent grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of granted patents split between resident and non-resident applicants over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows composition of grants in terms of domestic vs foreign-origin rights. Note from report: share of non-resident patent grants remained more or less stable over the past six years, contrasting with rising share of non-resident filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total patent grants by patent office
rubrics_metrics.description: Trends in patent grants broken down by patent office (long-term and for selected offices/top 20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights which offices grant the most patents and long-term patterns (e.g., stable 1880–1950, upward after mid-1960s, acceleration from mid-1980s). In 2006 the five largest offices (USA, Japan, Korea, China, EPO) accounted for ≈76.5% of total patent grants. Declines in grants in some European national offices may reflect parallel national vs regional (EPO) routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of resident and non-resident patent grants by office
rubrics_metrics.description: For each patent office, the share of grants going to resident and to non-resident applicants (e.g., 2006 office-level breakdown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveals variation across offices: e.g., non-resident grant share ranges from 99% in Hong Kong (SAR) to 10.3% in Japan. High non-resident shares indicate offices serving many foreign applicants; low shares indicate predominantly domestic-granted patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total patent grants by country of origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts, shares and growth rates of patents granted to applicants from each country (top origins, 2006).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify which countries' applicants receive the most patents. Example insights: in 2006 Japan (≈217,000 grants) and USA and Korea received substantial numbers; China and Korea showed significant growth 2000–2006. Combined shares of top origins can indicate concentration levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents in force (by country of origin and by patent office)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of patents currently in force aggregated by country of origin and by patent office (e.g., 2006 counts and comparisons to 2004).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the active stock of patent rights. Note that totals may be underestimated when origin is unknown (~0.5 million unknown in report). Observations: total patents in force ≈6.1 million in 2006; Japan and USA own the majority (≈1.6m and ≈1.2m respectively); largest number of patents in force by office is in the USA (≈1.8m). Differences between 'by origin' and 'by office' rankings can indicate presence of many foreign applicants in domestic markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age profile of patents in force (by year of filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of patents in force by their filing year (which shows cohorts and how many remain in force for each filing year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps assess how long patents are maintained and renewal behavior. Example: more than half of patents in force in 2006 were filed between 1997 and 2003. Maintenance/renewal schedules affect profile (e.g., USPTO maintenance fees due at 3.5, 7.5 and 11.5 years). Only a minority of patents are maintained for the full 20-year term from filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model filings (by patent office, resident/non-resident)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and distribution of utility model filings across patent offices and the split between resident and non-resident filings (e.g., 2000 vs 2006).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility models are an alternative IP right with shorter terms and less stringent examination than patents; they are mainly used for domestic protection. Example: China received 161,366 utility model filings in 2006; non-resident share is typically low (0.8% in China up to 20.9% in Austria). Trends and cross-office comparisons indicate where utility models are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model grants (by patent office, resident/non-resident)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and distribution of utility model grants across patent offices and resident/non-resident shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows where utility models are being issued. Example: China issued 107,655 utility model grants in 2006; non-resident grant shares vary widely (1.2% in China to 22.9% in Mexico). Trends over time show where grants are increasing or decreasing by office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent filings (trends and by patent office)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total resident patent filings over time and their distribution among patent offices (top offices, 1963–2006).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks domestic filing activity and long-term trends. Example: total resident filings ≈994,525 in 2006 (3.1% increase); since mid-1990s upward trend with peaks 1997–2000 and 2003–2006. Note: filings at the EPO are treated as non-resident in this report because they are often preceded by national filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent filings by country of origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts, shares and growth rates of resident filings by applicants from each country (top 20 origins, 2006).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to see domestic filing intensity by origin. Example: Japan led in resident filings (347,060 in 2006) followed by the USA, Korea and China. European country shares may be underestimated because of direct EPO filings being counted as non-resident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent grants (trends and by patent office)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time series and office-level distribution for patents granted to resident applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows domestic grant activity and trends; more volatile than filings due to office processing resources. Example: ≈407,864 resident patents granted worldwide in 2006 (22.5% increase). Top five offices accounted for 85.8% of resident grants in 2006.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent grants by country of origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts, shares and year-on-year growth of patents granted to residents of each country (top origins, 2006).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows comparison of which countries' residents receive the most patents domestically and their growth patterns. Example: Japan residents received the largest number of resident grants in 2006 (126,804). Note European totals may be understated because EPO grants are counted as non-resident in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-resident patent filings (trends and by patent office)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time series of filings by non-resident applicants and their distribution across patent offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates where applicants seek protection abroad and which offices attract foreign filings. Example: total non-resident filings ≈770,109 in 2006 (7.4% increase); the USPTO received >200,000 non-resident filings in 2006. Non-resident filings grew faster than resident filings in recent years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-resident patent filings by country of origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and shares of non-resident filings originating from each country (top origins, 2006).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows which countries file abroad most often. Example: largest non-resident filing origins in 2006 were the USA (169,031) and Japan (166,987). Rapid recent increases in non-resident filings from China are noted (avg. annual growth >30% for 2000–2006).

rubrics_metrics.name: European intra-regional filings by office
rubrics_metrics.description: Intra-regional indicator: filings by residents of EPC countries at European offices, showing counts by office (2006).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows preference of EPC residents when protecting inventions in the European region. Example: the EPO accounted for 87.6% of EPC countries’ intra-regional filings — applicants prefer the EPO to national offices for protection across EPC states.

rubrics_metrics.name: European extra-regional filings by office
rubrics_metrics.description: Extra-regional indicator: filings at European offices by non-EPC applicants (2006), with office-level breakdown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows where non-EPC applicants choose to protect inventions in Europe. Example: the EPO accounted for 78.6% of extra-regional filings, a lower share than for intra-regional filings; Germany and the UK have higher shares of extra-regional filings than intra-regional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-resident patent grants (trends and by patent office)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time series and office-level distribution of patents granted to non-resident applicants (1985–2006, and selected offices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks cross-border grant activity. Example: non-resident grants rose from ≈177,617 in 1985 to ≈319,429 in 2006; in 2006 the USPTO issued the largest number of non-resident patents (83,947). Growth patterns often mirror non-resident filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-resident patent grants by country of origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and shares of non-resident grants received by applicants from each country (top origins, 2006).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates which origin countries receive the most grants abroad. Example: applicants from Japan (28.4%) and the USA (20.3%) received the largest shares of non-resident grants in 2006. Emerging countries may have low non-resident grant rankings relative to their domestic office rankings, indicating limited patenting activity abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT international filings (trends, 1985-2007)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trends in Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) international filings over time (1985–2007) and year-on-year growth rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure internationalization of patenting via the PCT route. Example: total PCT filings in 2007 ≈158,400 (5.9% increase); PCT filings grew rapidly until 2001 then slowed. The USA is the largest PCT user (≈33.6% in 2006), followed by Japan (≈17.5%).

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT filings by country of origin and average annual growth rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Country-level shares of PCT filings in a given year (e.g., 2007) and average annual growth rates over periods (e.g., 2000–2007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows which countries rely most on PCT for seeking international protection and which countries' PCT use is growing fastest (e.g., increases for Japan, Korea, China; relative decrease for the USA over 2000–2006).

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT filings by ownership type (business/university/government/others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of PCT filings across ownership categories (business, university, government, others) by country and over time (2002–2007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illuminates sectoral composition of international patenting. Useful for comparing countries' PCT users by sector and for identifying leading sectors in PCT activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top PCT applicants by sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists and counts of the leading PCT applicants in the business and university sectors (e.g., top applicants in 2007 and comparisons to 2005).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for identifying leading corporate and academic filers internationally. Data typically presented as rankings and counts across years to show changes in applicant activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average annual growth rates as a comparative metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Average annual growth rates computed for various indicators (e.g., filings, grants, PCT filings) over specified periods (e.g., 2000–2006, 2000–2007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare growth dynamics across countries, offices, and indicator types. Report notes e.g., non-resident filings grew 7.3% p.a. between 1994–2006; China had >30% avg. annual growth in non-resident filings for 2000–2006.
